dissertation.title: From Perception to Clinical Reasoning: Disentangled, Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Learning for Robust Medical Image Analysis and Reporting
dissertation.summary: Reading a medical image involves five judgments: locating a finding, grading it, weighing it against clinical context, comparing it with earlier studies, and committing to a claim. This dissertation builds methods for each stage on two ideas: every stage carries a distribution rather than a point estimate, and evidence from different sources is represented separately so that losing one source does not corrupt the others. It is evaluated across endoscopy, whole-slide histology, retinal photography, brain MRI with genomics, and chest radiography.

stages.name: Contextualization
stages.question: Which source supports the reading, and what if context is missing?

stages.name: Comparison
stages.question: How has the finding changed since the prior study?

stages.name: Commitment
stages.question: Can the claim be checked against the image?

thesis.title: Attentive Multi-modal Learning: Unifying Visual and Clinical Insights for Medical Image Classification and Report Generation
thesis.summary: Integrates medical images, clinical text and genetics through scalable attention networks and vision-language models. Introduces Spatial Sequence Attention (SSA) for schizophrenia diagnosis from structural MRI, the Multi-modal Imaging Genomics Transformer (MIGTrans) that adds functional connectivity and SNP genomics, and the Multi-Modal Medical Transformer (M3T) for retinal report generation.

themes.title: Structured multimodal perception
themes.text: Modality-aware attention and fusion that respect how clinical data is structured.

themes.title: Robust latent disentanglement
themes.text: Probabilistic factorization so models degrade gracefully under missing modalities, class imbalance and representation collapse.

themes.title: Uncertainty-aware longitudinal reasoning
themes.text: Disease progression as distributional change, with temporal claims tied to image evidence.
